title.en: Deploying Lightweight FastAPI Microservices with Docker Swarm on Local Cloud
title.id: Deploy Microservices FastAPI Ringan Menggunakan Docker Swarm di Cloud Lokal

desc.en: Why Kubernetes is overkill for 95% of Indonesian startups: managing 8 distributed microservices on a $40/month local VPS cluster.
desc.id: Mengapa Kubernetes terlalu kompleks untuk 95% startup: mengelola 8 microservices di cluster VPS lokal seharga $40/bulan.

body.en:
Why Kubernetes is overkill for 95% of Indonesian startups: managing 8 distributed microservices on a $40/month local VPS cluster.

The Kubernetes Complexity Trap for Lean Teams

Setting up managed EKS or GKE clusters incurs significant baseline costs: control plane fees, multi-AZ load balancers, and dedicated DevOps maintenance overhead. For teams under 20 engineers, this operational complexity drains product momentum.

8microservices orchestrated smoothly
$40/mototal VPS hosting cost (Biznet/IDCloudHost)
99.95%uptime across rolling deploys

Docker Swarm as the Pragmatic Alternative

Docker Swarm is built directly into standard Docker engines. With zero additional control-plane agents, it provides overlay networking, automatic DNS service discovery, and declarative rolling updates across cheap Indonesian cloud instances (Biznet GIO, IDCloudHost).

Zero-Downtime Deployments with start-first Updates

By configuring update_config with start-first ordering and health checks, Swarm brings up new FastAPI containers and verifies HTTP 200 health responses before tearing down legacy instances, completely eliminating deployment drops.

Zero-Downtime Rolling Update Definition
version: "3.8"
services:
  api-gateway:
    image: registry.gitlab.com/albertus/core-api:latest
    deploy:
      replicas: 3
      update_config:
        parallelism: 1
        delay: 10s
        order: start-first
        failure_action: rollback
      restart_policy:
        condition: on-failure
    ports:
      - "8000:8000"
    networks:
      - internal-mesh

Centralized Logging and Observability with Loki

Pairing Grafana Loki and Promtail with the Swarm cluster provides unified, searchable log aggregation across all service nodes while consuming less than 250MB of host memory.
